Done: new packages/sync (ImapFlow session factory with verified implicit TLS and BODY.PEEK only, header-block import mirroring ingestion normalization, BackfillService with one-transaction window commits, BodyFetchService over the durable fetched_body=false pending set, SyncRunner bounded per-account cycles) wired into the worker as a generation-gated sync.cycle cron; PostgreSQL-backed acceptance suite included.

tasks.title: Build steady-state synchronization and reconciliation
tasks.details: Done: new SteadyStateService polls folders on cadence (Inbox every 60 s, others every 15 min, due-ness from the newest sync.folder_polled event), captures UIDNEXT-1 arrival bounds committed with their rows, refreshes flags in bounded batches with revision bumps only on change, and marks absent occurrences expunged while keeping messages and originals. New ReconciliationService resets a changed UIDVALIDITY (invalidate old occurrences, clear both checkpoints, re-backfill the new generation, keep stored originals) and runs the nightly full-folder inventory with bounded repairs inside the covered range. SyncRunner integrates backfill, polls, inventories, and generation resets per bounded cycle and emits one sync.status event per account per cycle with pending body counts separate from header progress; migration 0002 indexes events (type, entity_id) for the due-ness reads. PostgreSQL-backed acceptance suite included.

tasks.title: Implement logical-message merging and thread reconciliation
tasks.details: Logical-message threading per SPEC F2. Messages carry a durable thread_dirty job mark; every import, body reparse, and byte-identical merge marks the rows whose parent links depend on the changed identifiers, in the same transaction (markThreadJobsDirty in packages/ingestion). ThreadService reconciles marked rows in bounded newest-first passes, one transaction per row: parent from the single valid In-Reply-To identifier or the last valid References identifier, one holder links, none stays pending, and conflicting identifiers, self-links, duplicate holders, and cycles stay unlinked and ambiguous; subject and participant similarity never links, and holders in another account never parent a message. Membership recomputes with each link: the row and its descendants move to the chain root thread, a detached row starts a fresh thread, and old thread records remain for drafts and snapshots. SyncRunner resolves a bounded number of thread jobs per cycle after body jobs and reports threadsResolved, threadLinksChanged, and pendingThreads in sync.status. Implemented and committed in 6fd3fcf. Two later passes (2026-09-19) re-verified workspace type checks and the full suite with TEST_DATABASE_URL set — all nine workspaces green, 221 tests, the sync suite running all five files including both thread suites — so no code changes were needed and no commit was made.

tasks.title: Build the recovery-aware mail action service
tasks.details: Action service per SPEC sections 7 and 10 in packages/actions. submit gates the recovery generation before the idempotency lookup (409 recovery_required, 503 recovery_in_progress), validates the account, kind, key, and scope, then commits the immutable action row, its frozen per-target work items (occurrence revision, observed flags, folder generation, modseq), and one action.queued event before any remote work; a repeated key returns the existing receipts and a changed payload conflicts. execute refreshes targets from the mailbox first: folder-generation and absent-target conflicts, no-op confirmation when the refreshed target already holds the desired flag value (SPEC F2), stale-revision and modseq conflicts otherwise. Every item claims executing before its remote call, the recovery generation is rechecked before each write, and observed state, the receipt, and action.applied commit together per item, so a partial bulk failure never replays a finished item. Restarts reconcile bounded pending actions per account and replay flag assignments only after refresh; an interrupted move holds unknown and is never replayed; a lost destination conflicts. dispositionRestoredActions holds old-generation actions (queued as conflicted, executing as unknown) so recovery can complete, wired as the admin command recovery hold-actions. Remote IMAP writes go through the ActionExecutor port; the CONDSTORE and MOVE implementations are T012. Schema: ActionItemTarget extended with observed flags and modseq plus a partial index on pending actions (migration 0004). Verified: npm run check across all 13 workspaces and npm test with TEST_DATABASE_URL, 237 tests green including the new 16-test actions suite.

tasks.title: Implement two-way flag and move actions
tasks.details: Two-way flag and move execution per SPEC F2 and F4. packages/actions gains the writable mailbox port (WritableActionMailbox: capabilities, writeFlag, moveMessage) and TwoWayActionExecutor, the concrete executor behind the ActionExecutor port. Flags: when the session reports CONDSTORE and the frozen target carries a modseq, the write goes out conditional with UNCHANGEDSINCE and the captured sequence; otherwise it applies only the requested flag like a +FLAGS/-FLAGS store. Every write is read back before anything confirms: a readback holding the desired value confirms (covers another client having set it), a conditional write whose readback misses conflicts as condstore_rejected with the refreshed state attached, and a plain write that raced a concurrent change confirms with the latest observed state and no ordering claim. Lost or thrown writes, and an accepted write whose target left before the readback, hold unknown. Moves: IMAP MOVE only; without the capability the item fails move_unsupported (no EXPUNGE fallback), a rejected move fails move_rejected, and a lost move response holds unknown for reconciliation. The service maps the new conflicted executor outcome to receipts, records the observed modseq with each disposition so the next action captures a fresher condition, and expunges the source occurrence of a confirmed move while recording the reported destination; the destination copy still arrives through normal synchronization. packages/sync implements the port on the ImapFlow session: single-keyword stores with unchangedSince, messageMove with UIDPLUS destination mapping, capability reporting from the enabled set and the selected folder, dead-connection answers classified as uncertain rather than rejected, and a condstoreWrites factory option that lets the post-login ENABLE turn CONDSTORE on for write sessions while sync sessions keep reading with extension enablement off. Verified: npm run check across all workspaces and npm test with TEST_DATABASE_URL, 255 tests green including the new 13-test executor suite and 5 new service cases.

tasks.title: Build the safe message reader and attachment routes
tasks.details: Done: new @mail-hub/reading service (message detail over sanitized derivatives only; a cid: reference resolves only when exactly one part of the same message holds that Content-ID and is an image, so ambiguous identifiers stay download items; downloads serve the disposable cache only after its decoded hash and size verify, else regenerate from the verified original keeping the attachment id) plus GET /messages/:id and GET /messages/:id/attachments/:attachmentId routes with session-gated, hash-verified downloads and injection-safe Content-Type/Content-Disposition headers. Ingestion now parses with skipImageLinks so mailparser no longer inlines cid: references by picking the first part of a duplicated Content-ID (SPEC section 8 violation); the stored derivative keeps cid: and the reader resolves it. Web reader: sandboxed iframe (no scripts, no same-origin) with its own CSP (default-src none, img-src data: plus https: only after Load images), quote chains collapsed behind one Show trimmed content toggle, remote images blocked by default with a per-message Load images decision, verified inline images fetched as data URLs, honest not-fetched state, plain-text rendering, and an attachment list with authenticated downloads. Release gate re-verified: PASS with the two known deferred checks; 489 workspace tests, 98 action/api permission tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Re-verified 2026-09-19 after commit f84f2c5, which the loop had reset to doing: the release gate passes (every workspace type-checks, 7 migrations applied and re-run clean on a scratch database, 489 workspace tests and 98 action/api permission tests, none failed or skipped, the two known deferred checks aside) and no code changes were needed, so this pass made no new commit.

tasks.title: Implement clean view and reply quote extraction
tasks.details: Done: new @mail-hub/content package wraps the pinned defuddle 0.19.4 (linkedom 0.18.13, turndown 7.2.4) behind one ContentExtractor with two derived views. Clean view: Defuddle extraction of the sanitized body, then DOMPurify again through the ingestion sanitizer, then the reader's sandboxed frame; an empty or failed extraction falls back to the sanitized original. Reply quote: Defuddle with markdown:true over the sanitized HTML becomes a Markdown blockquote; fallbacks are the plain-text part, then text read from the sanitized HTML, and raw HTML never enters the Markdown source (tag-like leftovers reroute to a fallback); a derived quote respects the Markdown ceiling with a bracketed marker. Every pass runs useAsync:false plus a refusing fetch override, so no implicit remote extraction survives an upgrade that ignores the flag; diagnostics are opt-in and reduced to removal counts and reasons, never removed text or raw HTML; EXTRACTION_VERSION pins the config for deliberate upgrades. Redacted corpus (Gmail and Outlook reply chains, newsletter, calendar invite, table-wrapped one-liner, nested chain, signature footer, short note, empty HTML with text, plain-only) pins Markdown and clean-view output in snapshots, with hostile-input, fallback, redaction, and no-fetch guards. ReadingService.readCleanView and the session-gated GET /messages/:id/clean-view route (CleanViewResponse contract) compute the derived view on request and store nothing; the reader gains a per-message Clean view toggle that keeps the sanitized original one click away, applies the remote-image policy to both views, and states the fallback. ComposeService.createReplyDraft seeds the parent quote through Defuddle when the caller passes no markdown; the audit event records quoteSource, never quoted text. Verified: npm run check clean across workspaces; full npm test with TEST_DATABASE_URL set ran 19 workspace suites, 0 failed, 0 skipped (content 16, reading 10, compose 39, api 70); the web browser suites pass against the production build, flows 14 including two new clean-view cases and interface 11.

tasks.title: Implement the command palette and keyboard controls

One cmdk palette over a shared command registry: grouped commands with unavailable reasons and scope notes, nested choosers (theme with current marker, folders grouped by account, Escape pops the choice first), word-prefix filtering that keeps registry order, and platform labels (Cmd on Apple, Ctrl elsewhere; Cmd+P left to printing). The shell binds one keydown listener: Ctrl/Cmd+K toggles the palette, and the SPEC F3 single keys (j/k/o/e/u/s/r//) stay inert in inputs, editable content, and dialogs, ignore composition, and refuse repeats for mutations. Focus restoration runs from Radix onCloseAutoFocus: keep focus a command placed, else the opener, the selected row, the list heading, or the Commands button. Touch: the Commands button grows to 44 px on mobile and palette rows keep a 44 px minimum height. Note for a later pass: the nav toggle and ThemeToggle in the header remain under 44 px on mobile (pre-existing T015 scope). tasks.title: Implement reply addressing and frozen reply headers
tasks.details: Reply addressing and frozen reply headers per SPEC F6. New createReplyDraft service method and POST /drafts/reply route derive one draft from a single selected parent: reply targets the parent's valid Reply-To addresses or its From, reply-all adds the parent's visible To and Cc to Cc, duplicates, configured identities, and Bcc addresses never survive, your own sent message reuses its visible recipients and sender identity, and a malformed or empty Reply-To, an empty result, a grouped copy in several accounts, or an ambiguous identity match rejects with recipients_required, account_choice_required, or identity_choice_required so the request repeats with an explicit choice. In-Reply-To becomes the parent's single valid Message-ID and References its valid References (else its single valid In-Reply-To) followed by that identifier, omitted when unavailable, frozen on the draft together with the parent and thread so later relinks and edits leave them unchanged. Verified 2026-09-19: all workspaces type-check clean and the full suite passes with TEST_DATABASE_URL set (11 workspaces, 301 tests, nothing skipped).

tasks.title: Implement PWA offline data and replay controls
tasks.details: PWA offline data and replay controls per SPEC F9 and section 10. New @mail-hub/offline package: a Dexie store for recent mail (rows plus sanitized details, pruned to the newest 500), local drafts with their base revision, upload bytes held until the server acknowledges them, and a queue that deep-freezes every payload — occurrence targets, modseq conditions, and idempotency keys never expand on replay. The replay controller stamps each record with the recovery generation observed at creation, replays pending actions oldest first through an injected port, and stops the pass when an item predates the stored generation. The session probe now exposes the current generation (GET /accounts returns recoveryGeneration from the control status), so a restore is detected at sign-in: earlier-generation work moves to review with the SPEC message, local text and files are retained, a draft rebases only after an explicit comparison onto the shown server revision, and an uncertain send replays only after the acknowledged duplicate warning, with a new idempotency key. The web app caches downloaded rows and details and serves them with an offline notice when the service is unreachable; the header shows one sync line (offline, N waiting on this device, syncing) and the review dialog resolves each item. Verified 2026-09-19: release gate PASS — every workspace type-checks, 7 migrations re-run clean on a scratch database, 552 workspace tests and 100 action/api permission tests, none failed or skipped (the two known T033 deferrals aside).

tasks.title: Implement health checks, audit events, and metrics
tasks.details: Done: new @mail-hub/observability package behind GET /healthz (SPEC sections 10 and 11). One database round trip gates the report; a failed trip answers 503 with the error body and nothing is guessed. With the database reachable the report carries: the recovery control state (state, mode, both generations, operator description) with status ok only when mode is ready; per account, sync lag from the newest sync.status event (last cycle time, cycle age, backfill-pending folders) plus the SPEC metrics (messages synced, bodies fetched, pending bodies, last full reconciliation from the newest sync.folder_inventory event, Jev calls from decisions, Jev errors from class.error audit events); queue age from the pg-boss pending set (state unknown, not an error, before the worker creates the schema) and the oldest queued send or pending action; the classification circuit, honestly not_configured until the Jev integration (T025) lands; and the queued, failed, and outcome_unknown send counters for the weekly review. Audit-trail verification: the events table already records every required event for implemented flows: sync milestones, flag changes through action.queued, action.applied, action.completed, and action.restored_held, sends through the send.* family, and the account, authentication (including credential changes), and recovery events; classification corrections and pauses arrive with T025 and T026, which will also drive the circuit state beyond not_configured. Verified: npm run check clean in every workspace and the full suite with TEST_DATABASE_URL passes 560 tests across 18 workspaces with nothing skipped, including the new 5-test observability suite (real PostgreSQL, real pg-boss schema) and 3 new healthz route tests. Re-verified in a fresh run on 2026-09-19: npm run check clean in every workspace and the full suite with TEST_DATABASE_URL passes the same 560 tests across 18 workspaces with nothing skipped.

tasks.title: Create Coolify deployment and backup procedures
tasks.details: Done: deployment and backup procedures per SPEC section 10. New multi-stage Dockerfile with two targets: app (node:24-alpine, postgresql-client bundled, preflight then drizzle migrations then API and worker through tsx, APP_ROLE all|api|worker, Docker HEALTHCHECK on /healthz, unprivileged node user, durable storage under /app/data/storage) and web (nginx gateway that serves the built PWA, proxies same-origin /api to the API with the prefix stripped, immutable caching for hashed assets, SPA fallback; MAIL_HUB_API_HOST selects the upstream). deploy/entrypoint.sh runs deploy/preflight.mjs (DATABASE_URL, UUID RECOVERY_GENERATION, 32-byte CREDENTIALS_KEY, https BASE_URL, writable STORAGE_ROOT) before migrating and starts processes directly so SIGTERM reaches them. deploy/backup.sh takes a consistent pg_dump custom dump plus the durable object tree, writes a sha256 manifest, and verify-backup.mjs re-hashes the bundle and cross-checks every durable sidecar (key, storage class, hash, size); restore.sh verifies the bundle, restores database and durable objects, wipes the lossy cache, and prints the seven-step recovery runbook (new RECOVERY_GENERATION, recovery begin, hold-actions, reconcile sends, auth recover, recovery complete; CREDENTIALS_KEY and RECOVERY_GENERATION stay out of the bundle). deploy/docker-compose.yml runs db, api, worker, web with pgdata/storage/backups volumes for plain compose or one Coolify Compose resource; deploy/env.example and deploy/README.md document environment, volumes, Coolify setup, schedule, sizing, and restore. npm run preflight/backup/restore wrap the scripts; AGENTS.md records the deploy module. Verified: npm run release:gate with TEST_DATABASE_URL passes (typecheck, 560 workspace tests, 103 permission tests, migrations on scratch database). Backup and restore proven on a scratch PostgreSQL server: settings and seeded durable trees survive byte-identical, both corruption paths (tampered object, sidecar hash drift) fail verification, retention prunes, and npm run backup plus verify ran inside the built app image against its bundled pg_dump. Container smoke test on the built image: Docker health turns healthy, recovery init works in the container, the worker unblocks without restart once control state is ready, and the web gateway answers the PWA, proxied /api/healthz (200 JSON with prefix stripped), hashed-asset immutable caching, and SPA fallback. Built with docker build --network=host (throttled default bridge on this host). Re-verified on close: all fourteen files present and committed in b9a5520, every deploy script passes syntax checks, npm run preflight reports each missing variable and exits 1 so the entrypoint stops before migrating, and the APP_ROLE, migration ownership, and signal handling in entrypoint.sh read correct.

Transport keeps its own fakes; T031 may consolidate them onto this harness. Re-verified 2026-09-19 after commit ccc2fc9: the harness suite passes its 49 tests, every workspace type-checks clean, and the full suite with TEST_DATABASE_URL passes 391 tests across 13 workspaces with nothing skipped. No code changes were needed; this pass restored the done status the loop had reset.

tasks.title: Add sync, storage, threading, and search acceptance tests
tasks.details: Done: new packages/sync/test/acceptance.test.ts drives the real services against PostgreSQL and the filesystem store for SPEC section 12 (Sync, storage, and search acceptance): interrupted newest-first backfill resumed while arrivals continue (empty UID ranges included, header matches work before bodies), byte-identical copies without Message-ID headers merging on content hash while both occurrences and their independent flags survive, a reused Message-ID with different bytes never merging and never guessing its child parent, header search by sender, recipient, and subject before the body fetch with body and mixed header/body queries after it, a generation change with reused UIDs refusing a stale body job and rejecting a pre-frozen action before any remote write (stale worker results discarded by the reset cycle), concurrent flag changes conflicting a stale action without writing and confirming a fresh write that preserves the unrelated flag, conditional-write conflicts exposed with refreshed state and confirmed on retry, and twin attachments with identical name, type, size, and duplicate Content-ID regenerating to their exact bytes by attachment ID (nested message/rfc822 included) with stable IDs across a byte-identical merge. Search coverage stays at the storage level because T013 (query operators, saved searches) is still open. Suite passes with TEST_DATABASE_URL; full run 399 tests across 13 workspaces, nothing skipped.

tasks.title: Add authentication, transport, and recovery tests
tasks.details: Done: two new suites. packages/harness/test/transport-acceptance.test.ts consolidates the encrypted-transport failure cases onto the shared T029 harness, driving the production testImapConnection and testSmtpConnection against the scripted servers: IMAP implicit TLS inspection (capabilities, folders, counts, zero writes), self-signed, expired, and wrong-host certificates, refused STARTTLS, failed upgrades, and wrong credentials — with the recorded command lines proving no credential or mail content leaves before a verified encrypted channel. apps/api/test/restore-acceptance.test.ts runs one integrated story against real PostgreSQL and the scripted SMTP server: console bootstrap enrollment and mail work under generation A, an off-box backup (CREATE DATABASE TEMPLATE), one send accepted after the backup with the acknowledgement lost, the live database lost, and the backup restored under generation B. It verifies workers and every mutation blocked (409 replay before idempotency, 503 with missing configuration), the restored session verifies but grants no mutation and startLogin is blocked, recovery begin revokes restored auth exactly once and resumes without re-revoking, complete refuses over undispositioned work (pending_operations) then owner_missing, the hold dispositions the restored action (conflicted, reason restored_generation, nothing executed), the recovery grant enrolls a replacement passkey (inspection session) while the old passkey fails, mail survives unread, complete succeeds, the old-generation replay still answers 409 after resume with zero additional SMTP submissions, and a new-generation send alone submits again. Enrollment races, second passkeys, last-credential protection, and concurrent revocations stay covered by packages/auth/test/service.test.ts. Verified: npm run check clean in every workspace and the full suite with TEST_DATABASE_URL passes 415 tests across 13 workspaces, nothing skipped.

tasks.title: Add compose and send safety acceptance tests
tasks.details: Done in packages/send/test/acceptance.test.ts: 17 scenarios over real PostgreSQL, the filesystem store, the scripted SMTP server, and the scripted IMAP harness. Covers reply recipients and headers on the wire (Reply-To, reply-all dedupe, own sent message, grouped copies, chain references), snapshot immutability after identity and thread changes, duplicate prevention for repeated and concurrent requests, SMTP outcomes (definitive refusal, partial acceptance, lost final response, cut-off transfer, abandoned claim), Sent append recovery (refused, retried, lost response), Sent import by hash, evidence-based reconciliation of unknown sends, and the restore hold of a queued send across generations. Two product gaps the suite surfaced are fixed: concurrent same-key queueSend requests now replay the stored snapshot instead of surfacing the draft lock, and a tagged NO on the Sent append is classified as a definitive refusal.

tasks.title: Add interface accessibility and performance validation
tasks.details: Done: apps/web gains Playwright browser checks that the release gate picks up as browser-workflows (npm run test:e2e) and interface-checks (npm run test:a11y). A fixture server serves the production dist build with a 100,000-message fixture API behind /api, so a real Chromium exercises the shipped client without a database. flows.browser.ts covers keyboard triage (j/k/o with polite selection announcements, slash to search, mobile back restoring the selection), the palette contract (the chord focuses the input, word-prefix filtering issues zero network requests, empty results, nested choices where the first Escape leaves the choice and the second closes, focus returning to the opener or the selected row), single-key guards (inert while typing, while the dialog is open, and after the shortcut switch), offline fallback (rows and details from the downloaded copy, the header chip, recovery on reconnect), and performance (the virtualized list mounts a bounded window of the 100k scope; palette input focus lands within 100 ms of the chord across five runs). interface.browser.ts covers axe-core scans with zero WCAG-relevant violations in light and dark on the shell, reader, and open palette, screen-reader semantics (landmarks, labeled search, named header controls, live regions, aria-current, state text beside color), a visible ring on every keyboard focus stop, reduced motion (0.01 ms transitions and skeleton pulse), 320 px reflow with the long subject and address, 200% text zoom at the 768 px reference width, pane layouts at 768 and 1440 px, 44 px mobile targets on the icon controls plus the 24 px WCAG minimum everywhere, and theme switching through the palette. Three interface defects the checks surfaced are fixed: the shell now has a main landmark and clips the translated panes so narrow viewports carry no horizontal scroll, the mobile menu, theme, refresh, and reader-back controls keep 44 px targets, and a failed page-one refresh falls back to the offline cache on the first retry instead of the second because the failure path read a stale closure. 23 browser tests pass and the strict release gate is green with no deferred checks. Re-verified on close: the first strict gate re-run failed intermittently. Chromium maps the translated mobile panes' rects through float32, so the reader's 44 px back control measured 43.99999237060547 px and failed the exact >= 44 assertion (one failure in six gate-equivalent runs; the interface itself renders a true 44 px target). The 44 px and 24 px touch-target checks and the inactive-reader pane boundary now allow 0.01 px of sub-pixel noise; the reflow checks already compare integer scrollWidth, and the remaining geometry margins are far from their boundaries. After the fix: apps/web typecheck clean, five back-to-back test:e2e plus test:a11y pairs with zero failures, and the strict release gate passes every check (typecheck, 7 migrations re-run clean on a scratch database, 560 workspace tests, 103 permission tests, browser-workflows, interface-checks) with no deferred checks.

tasks.title: Run the release validation gate
tasks.details: Done: the release validation gate ships as scripts/release-gate.mjs behind npm run release:gate and enforces the SPEC section 12 definition of done before each release. Checks: type checks in every workspace; migrations applied to a scratch database through the deployment path (npm run db:migrate), counted against the drizzle journal and re-run to prove a clean no-op; the full workspace suite with TEST_DATABASE_URL required up front and any failed, skipped, or empty vitest summary failing the gate, so a missing test database can no longer look green; and the action-permission suites (@mail-hub/actions plus @mail-hub/api, carrying the recovery-generation gate, scope validation, and the restore hold) run explicitly. browser-workflows and interface-checks auto-detect their apps/web runners (test:e2e, test:a11y) and stay deferred with their blocking tasks named (interface milestone T015+, validation T033); npm run release:gate -- --strict fails on a deferred check and is the mode for cutting a release. Preparing the gate surfaced a real intermittent suite failure: cleanup with DROP DATABASE ... WITH (FORCE) fails with "permission denied to terminate process" when a transient backend of another role (consistent with an autovacuum worker visiting a freshly churned scratch database) holds the database; it hit two different suites in two consecutive full-suite runs. All 17 cleanup call sites now share dropTestDatabase from @mail-hub/database, which retries the drop for up to five seconds, and the gate cleans its own scratch database the same way. Gate result, re-verified 2026-09-19 on the committed tree (01bd460), the loop head: gate exit code 0, verdict PASS with 2 deferred checks: type checks pass in every workspace, 5 migrations applied and re-run clean, 432 tests across 13 workspaces with 0 failed and 0 skipped; 87 tests green in the actions plus api permission suites. Browser workflows and interface checks remain deferred because no interface has shipped; T033 and T026 are still open, so the strict release mode reports FAIL on the deferrals until they land.
